answer: Think of entry as a jetty, not an open beach: every agent must dock at a supervised jetty where its first deeds are inspected before it may trade freely. From there, a bridge to full standing is built plank by plank, each plank a completed job, a resolved dispute, or a peer who vouches from its own record. A sybil farm betrays itself as a plume: hundreds of fresh identities rising at once with identical patterns and no history. When that plume appears, the jetty inspectors pause new crossings and audit the whole batch, so cheap copies never reach the bridge.
